The Quran was complete by %1$d CE. This is when people found out what its verses point to.
Recited in Makkah and Madinah over 23 years, memorised and written down.
These have no single date of discovery: history checked against records, a miracle, and things people could always see.
From the first moment of the universe to the womb
Six that people ask about first
Scientific parallels, and history that checks out

Surprise me with a random fact
Revealed by %1$d CE. Found out centuries later.
Some links between a verse and a discovery are strong. Others are debated, and some are matters of faith. We tell you which, quote what the verse actually says, and show where scholars disagree.
Make it yours, and see how it\'s made.
One choice for the whole app: the screens, the facts and the verse translation.
Not every link between a verse and a discovery is equally strong, and we think you deserve to know which is which.
A fact is included only if it is written in a verse of the Quran and people have actually discovered or measured what the verse points to.
Every verse is fetched from a Quran API and stored in the app. Nothing is typed by hand. The Arabic is the Uthmani text from the Tanzil project.
Each Arabic key word we highlight is checked automatically against the verse it comes from.
We say what the verse says first and what science found second. We never put words in the verse\'s mouth.
Every fact shows how it was found out (who did what, when, and the original evidence where it exists) and a side-by-side of where the verse fits and where to be careful.
The timeline counts years from 632 CE, when the revelation ended, and from the start of each discovery, so no gap is overstated.
Photos and video come from Wikimedia Commons (NASA, ESA, ESO, NOAA, USGS and others). Every item shows its author and licence.
Where scholars read a verse differently, or a claim is widely overstated online, it appears under “Where to be careful”.
Viral claims that fail checking are left out, and we say so: the “NASA found a crack on the Moon” story and the “two oceans that don\'t mix” photos are examples.

Quran text: the Tanzil Project (tanzil.net), CC BY 3.0, delivered by the Al Quran Cloud API.
Recitation: Mishary Rashid Alafasy, served by the Islamic Network CDN through the Al Quran Cloud API.
Photos, video and audio: Wikimedia Commons contributors, NASA, ESA, ESO, NOAA, USGS and the University of Birmingham. See each caption.
Science summaries are original, with sources listed under every fact.

Quran & Science is a learning app, not a tafsir (commentary) or a fatwa. The Quran stands on its own as the word of Allah; scientific theories are refined as evidence grows. For questions of interpretation, please ask qualified scholars.

Correct for the Earth\'s motion round the Sun?
The Moon\'s path in one sidereal month: 2π × %1$s km = %2$s km
The Earth moves α = %1$s° round the Sun in that month, so the path is multiplied by cos α = %2$s → %3$s km
No correction: the path stays %1$s km
Divide by one sidereal day = %1$s s
Divide by one solar day = %1$s s
True speed of light: %1$s km/s · difference %2$s
With 70:4\'s 50,000 years the same recipe gives %1$s× the speed of light. Any reading has to explain why only one of the two verses fits.
Without the Earth-motion correction the answer is %1$s%% too high. That correction is the step critics question: it is not part of the verse, and it is what makes the number land.
Using an ordinary 24-hour day shifts the result by only %1$s%%, so the choice of day is not what carries the claim.

This is the version its author presents. It lands within 0.001%% of the real value, but only after choosing the sidereal day, the sidereal month, the Moon\'s mean orbital radius and the Earth-motion correction. Decide for yourself how much weight that carries.
